prompt: Which frameworks should you use to build AI agents (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel)?
completion:
Below is a “quick‑start cheat‑sheet” that lets you decide which of the four popular agent frameworks—**LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI,** and **Semantic Kernel**—is the right fit for your project, or whether you might combine them. > **TL;DR** > • **LangGraph** – best for low‑level, stateful, graph‑oriented agent workflows. > • **AutoGen** – great if you need a lightweight, “ChatGPT‑style” API with built‑in memory & multi‑agent dialogue. > • **CrewAI** – the go‑to for orchestrated, role‑based “crew” of LLM agents (team‑style). > • **Semantic Kernel** – ideal for enterprise, plug‑in‑rich, multi‑skill LLM orchestration (especially in the Microsoft stack). --- ## 1. Framework Snapshots | Framework | Primary Design Goal | Core Features | Typical Use‑Case | Language(s) | License | |-----------|---------------------|---------------|------------------|-------------|---------| | **LangGraph** | Graph‑centric stateful agent pipelines | • Node/Edge graph representation
• Persistent state & checkpoints
• Tool calling + custom callbacks | Complex workflows that require branching, loops, and fine‑grained state tracking (e.g., data‑collection pipelines, multi‑step reasoning) | Python | Apache‑2.0 | | **AutoGen** | Conversational agent “dialect” for LLMs | • Auto‑generated prompt engineering
• Memory & persona abstraction
• Auto‑launch of multiple LLMs | Rapid prototyping of chat‑style agents, e.g., customer‑support bots, collaborative writing assistants | Python, JavaScript (Node.js) | Apache‑2.0 | | **CrewAI** | Team‑based, role‑driven orchestration | • Pre‑built crew templates
• Role‑definition & task allocation
• Built‑in progress tracking | Projects where you want a “mini‑team” of agents (researcher, writer, validator) to split and recombine work | Python | MIT | | **Semantic Kernel** | Enterprise‑grade skill orchestration | • “Skill” abstraction (LLM, API, custom logic)
• Prompt template & chain management
• Azure/OpenAI integration & plug‑ins | Enterprise apps that need tightly coupled LLM logic with existing .NET/Java/Node services | .NET, Java, Python, JavaScript | MIT | --- ## 2. Feature‑by‑Feature Deep Dive | Feature | LangGraph | AutoGen | CrewAI | Semantic Kernel | |---------|-----------|---------|--------|-----------------| | **Graph model** | Full graph API (nodes, edges, branching, cycles). State is explicitly stored at edges. | Implicit “conversation graph” via message history; no explicit graph API. | Implicit “task graph” via crew roles & task queues. | Implicit skill‑chain graph, but with declarative “skill graph” templates. | | **State persistence** | Built‑in checkpointing, persistence to JSON/DB. | Memory stored in LLM memory objects; can be persisted to Redis, etc. | Task state tracked in Crew’s internal store. | Skill state is usually stateless; can be extended via external state managers. | | **Tool/External API integration** | `ToolNode` abstraction; can call any REST/graphQL/SQL tool. | `ToolAgent` abstraction; can plug in custom APIs. | `Skill` integration via `LLMSkill` wrapper. | `Skill` can wrap anything: REST, Azure Functions, .NET services. | | **Parallelism** | Explicit parallel edges; can run nodes concurrently. | Parallel agents are launched via `AgentPool`. | Crew agents run concurrently; can be limited by resource. | Skills can be executed in parallel within a chain. | | **User control** | Full control over node ordering, branching logic. | Control via high‑level prompts & persona. | Control via role definitions & task allocation. | Control via skill graph DSL. | | **Error handling** | Custom callbacks; retry logic per node. | Built‑in retry and “fallback” agents. | Crew manages task failures and re‑assignment. | Skill errors can be caught in catch blocks. | | **Testing & debugging** | Graph debugger, visualizer, unit‑testable nodes. | Inspect message logs; use `DebugAgent`. | Crew has logging per agent & crew. | Use the `Trace` API to see skill calls. | --- ## 3. Scenario‑Based Recommendations | Scenario | Recommended Framework(s) | Why | |----------|--------------------------|-----| | **You need a workflow with many decision points, loops, and persistent checkpoints** | **LangGraph** | Its explicit graph model and state checkpoints are perfect for branching pipelines. | | **Rapid prototyping of a conversational chatbot that can ask clarifying questions** | **AutoGen** | AutoGen’s “prompt‑first” design lets you quickly build a dialog flow without writing a lot of plumbing. | | **You want a team of agents, each with a distinct role, to work together on a document** | **CrewAI** | CrewAI’s crew templates (writer, reviewer, summarizer) let you define roles once and scale out. | | **You’re building a production‑grade enterprise app on Azure that needs to combine LLM calls with existing .NET services** | **Semantic Kernel** | Its “skills” can wrap .NET services, and it integrates natively with Azure OpenAI and other Microsoft tools. | | **You need to mix the best of each (e.g., a graph workflow that calls a crew of agents)** | **Combine** | LangGraph for the graph + a custom node that invokes a CrewAI crew, or an AutoGen agent that orchestrates Semantic Kernel skills. | --- ## 4. “Stack” Choices for Common Platforms | Stack | Preferred Agent Framework | Notes | |-------|--------------------------|-------| | **Python only** | LangGraph (for pipelines), AutoGen (for chat), CrewAI (for teams) | All three have mature Python SDKs. | | **Node.js / TypeScript** | AutoGen (JS variant) | LangGraph & CrewAI have experimental JS support; Semantic Kernel has JS SDK. | | **.NET / C#** | Semantic Kernel | Native, strong tooling, tight Azure integration. | | **Hybrid (Python + .NET)** | Semantic Kernel + AutoGen | Use Semantic Kernel to expose .NET skills to a Python AutoGen agent. | | **Low‑latency microservice** | AutoGen or LangGraph | AutoGen’s lightweight runtime; LangGraph’s async graph execution. | --- ## 5. Key Trade‑Offs to Consider | Factor | LangGraph | AutoGen | CrewAI | Semantic Kernel | |--------|-----------|---------|--------|-----------------| | **Learning curve** | Moderate (graph DSL) | Low (chat‑style) | Moderate (crew DSL) | Moderate (skill DSL) | | **Community & Ecosystem** | Growing (OpenAI‑focused) | Growing (LLM‑agnostic) | Medium (GitHub) | Mature (Microsoft) | | **Performance** | Optimized for large pipelines | Good for small to medium chats | Good for team tasks | Good for enterprise workloads | | **Extensibility** | Very high (custom nodes) | High (custom agents) | High (custom skills) | High (custom skills & connectors) | | **Compliance / Auditing** | Full control over logs & checkpoints | Depends on LLM provider | Full crew logs | Full traceability via Kernel’s trace API | --- ## 6. Quick‑Start Decision Flow 1. **Is your main goal a *conversation* with dynamic memory?** → **AutoGen** (fast prototyping). 2. **Do you need *multiple agents* working in parallel, each with a distinct role?** → **CrewAI** (crew templates). 3. **Do you require a *complex workflow* with branching, loops, and persistent state?** → **LangGraph** (graph model). 4. **Are you targeting an *enterprise* deployment with Azure/.NET stack?** → **Semantic Kernel** (skills + Azure integration). 5. **Do you need to combine the above (e.g., a graph that launches a crew of agents)?** → Build a custom integration: use LangGraph as the orchestrator, with a node that calls a CrewAI crew or a Semantic Kernel skill. --- ## 7. Next Steps 1. **Prototype**: Start with a minimal example (e.g., a 2‑node LangGraph or a 1‑agent AutoGen script). 2. **Profile**: Measure latency, memory usage, and error rates. 3. **Iterate**: Add roles or skills, then benchmark. 4. **Deploy**: Use containerization (Docker) + orchestration (K8s) and secure your LLM keys. --- ### Useful Links - **LangGraph** – - **AutoGen** – - **CrewAI** – - **Semantic Kernel** – Feel free to reach out if you want a deeper dive into a particular framework, or if you need code snippets for your specific use case!
